prospect.name: Jerry Harding
prospect.occupation: Railroad — positive train control representative, 12-hour shifts; previously 14 years as a 'diesel doc' remote diagnostics analyst
prospect.family_status: Married; one son aged 30, a 7-year-old granddaughter, 25 nieces and nephews plus roughly 10 great-nieces/nephews; youngest of eight
prospect.training_background: Very experienced and self-directed. Built a home gym in his basement: kettlebells, extensive weighted/resistance jump ropes, pull-up bar, dips, hip sled. Trains on a 'Texas two-step' rotation — two days on, two days off around 12-hour shifts, plus two three-day weekends a month. Does 120 'air push-ups' spread across the workday. Practises 16-20h intermittent fasting, one meal a day.
prospect.medical: Prostate cancer — prostate surgically removed and radiation treatment; reports quarterly blood work undetectable (0.0) for five-plus years. Resulting weak pelvic floor and mild incontinence. Former type 2 diabetes and hypertension, states both resolved and takes no medication. Sleep apnea. Chronic short sleep, 5-5.5 hours. Right pectoral injury (self-described bruise/inflammation, not a tear) still healing; treating it with self-administered BPC-157 peptide injections and has stopped bench pressing. Avoids TRT deliberately because of the cancer history. Takes lab-prescribed vitamins and minerals.

signals: Lost ground to serious illness — prostate cancer with surgery and radiation, plus diabetes and hypertension — and frames training as reclaiming capacity: 'if I can't run a mile flat out, or I can't jump rope for five minutes solid like I used to be able to, then those are the basic things that I need to work'
Wants a former self back rather than a first-time transformation: 'I want to be lean and ripped, and I want to learn how to swim'

Tension with the_preserver: he is older and health-literate, but he is NOT medically managed (takes no medication) and his goal is explicitly to gain leanness and capability, not merely hold on to function
Not the_prehab_fighter: the cancer is in remission five-plus years, not an active health event being fought

goals.text: Get lean and strip the remaining subcutaneous fat off stomach, chest and sides — wants to see a six-pack and lose the love handles
Drop from about 210 lb to around 185 lb
Keep and improve mobility and flexibility so everyday movement — walking, bending, stooping, carrying groceries — stays easy at 70
Functional strength he can apply to real life rather than gym numbers — running, jumping, swimming, picking things up
Be around and physically capable to see his 7-year-old granddaughter grow into a woman, through high school and college
Be a living example to his 30-year-old son, nieces and nephews of what discipline and strength look like
Learn to swim, travel to Asia and swim in the ocean, ride his off-road fat-tyre bikes — 'take this newfound youth and do something with it'
Stop chasing new methods and finally stay with one system long enough for it to work

pains.text: Stuck on a plateau he cannot break through despite discipline and consistency — 'I reach a certain point, and my body says, boom, we stop right here'
Sleeps only five to five and a half hours a night, has sleep apnea and a family history of insomnia; names sleep as the single biggest thing holding him back — 'without that factor, nothing works'
Information overload from social media — sees one good idea, then five more, and switches paths before anything compounds
Recovery is slower at 70 and he has historically overtrained into the ground — 'I was working myself beyond the ability to recover. Without recovery, you have no progression'
Weak pelvic floor and mild incontinence following prostate removal and radiation for prostate cancer
Right pectoral injury that made him stop bench pressing, currently being treated with peptide injections
Twelve-hour shifts leave nothing in the tank — he cannot train on workdays and eats all meals at work
Impatience — 'I want it yesterday' — which he identifies as sabotaging his own consistency
Everything he has bought has been cookie-cutter and not tuned to him as an individual: 'they're saying one size fits all and I know that's not true'
Background stress from the social and political climate, which he links to his sleep and recovery
Expects to be rejected by coaches for his age and profile — 'a lot of people during things like this have said, well, I don't think I can help you, Jerry, because they want the perfect candidate'

objections.raw_quote: But what I would say is, let me have it for Monday. Let's make Monday the deciding. I have one more thing. I have a guy that also I have been following for a long time. don't know if you've ever heard of Marcus of Philly.
objections.rep_response: Did not treat it as a price objection. Asked whether anything other than the Trevor-vs-Marcus decision had to be resolved, asked which way he was leaning, asked repeatedly what Marcus's argument was, and reflected back that the two coaches were saying the same thing so the differentiator was kettlebell specialisation. Eventually improvised a paid one-month trial as a way to resolve the comparison experientially.

objections.raw_quote: Can I, can I take 24 hours and call you back tomorrow or Sunday and we'll do the month? We'll do the month. We'll try it.
objections.rep_response: Accepted the delay and booked a follow-up call for Sunday at 11:00 Central, duplicating the existing Zoom link. Did not run the scripted 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is' sequence.

objections.raw_quote: I have to talk to my counterpart who is the, she is the, how can I put it, she's the bad guy and I'm the good guy, like the bad cop and the good cop
objections.rep_response: Asked whether she was supportive of him getting fitness dialled in, asked what her motivation would be for wanting him healthy, and asked what her potential concerns would be. Established she was supportive and had already estimated the price. Did not challenge whether this was genuinely her decision or ask whose responsibility it was.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Improvised on the call as a 'love it or leave it' programme: $1,200 up front for one month of full access (onboarding with Trevor, coaching calls, community), then a $4,800 balance at the end of the month to continue for the remaining term, or walk away with no further obligation.
offer.guarantee_mentioned: Framed as a walk-away rather than a refund: 'And if you go in and you're having second... Thoughts and you're second-guessing, then great, you leave it. At the end of the month, you say, hey, I'm going to go with Marcus... and we shake hands and part ways.'

evidence: No payment was taken. The rep collected legal name, billing address, email and phone and asked for a card — 'For the investment, did you want to do Visa, MasterCard, Amex, what works best on that side of things?' — and the prospect deferred: 'I'm probably going to put it on a Visa. Okay. But what I would say is, let me have it for Monday.'
No payment link was sent, so the verbal-agreement-plus-link close rule does not apply.
Follow-up call explicitly booked: 'How about 11 on Sunday?' … 'Sunday at 11. I'll be there.'

Counter-evidence, strongly positive: the prospect verbally agreed to the trial — 'Can I take 24 hours and call you back tomorrow or Sunday and we'll do the month? We'll do the month. We'll try it.' — and closed the call with 'Oh, Mike, I'm not going to change my mind.'
Counter-evidence: price met no resistance at all. 'I was thinking five. I had my wife speculating, you know, they're going to want about five grand... So that sounds really in the ballpark.'
Counter-evidence the other way: an active, directly comparable competitor was still in play at the end of the call — 'It's deciding between the two of them.'
outcome.next_step: Follow-up Zoom on Sunday 2026-07-05 at 11:00 Central on the same link, after the prospect compares Primal Instinct against Marcus Filly and speaks with his wife. Intended outcome is the $1,200 one-month start.

notable.note: Two things a manager needs to see on this call. First, the medical picture: a 70-year-old prostate cancer survivor with the prostate removed, radiation history, a weak pelvic floor with incontinence, sleep apnea and a still-healing pectoral injury under self-administered peptide injections was taken all the way to a card request without anyone asking whether a doctor had cleared him for loaded ballistic kettlebell work. He is explicitly counting on kettlebells to fix the pelvic floor — 'what attracts me to kettlebells is the core development of the movements and the fact that I'll strengthen my pelvic floor' — which is a clinical claim nobody qualified. Second, the price: when the prospect deferred, the rep invented a $1,200 one-month entry with a $4,800 balance and described it as a programme the company does not openly discuss. Separately, the prospect named sleep as his number one blocker and the three-pillar presentation never mentioned sleep once.

quality.notes: Severe and continuous. Whole rep turns are attributed to 'jerryharding' and vice versa throughout — for example the rep's own discovery questions ('You're 70 years old.', 'What's your current height and weight?', 'Cool. What's your diet look like right now?') appear under the prospect's label, and the prospect's answers appear under the rep's. Roles here were resolved entirely from content: the rep is whoever asks the discovery questions, delivers the three pillars and quotes the price. Line-level attribution in this file should not be trusted for anything.
